meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Then on what basis did you enter it?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People write in one place and paste into another. Did anyone ask Owen where he drafted it before November 3?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
That's not what I asked. Was Owen heard before the zero went in, yes or no?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Editions differ, and students misremember lines. And that's twice you've stepped around my question, Hale: was he heard first?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then I'll take your silence as a no. Your own procedure, 4.1, says you speak with the student first.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft; that's what an outline is for. And you still haven't answered 4.1.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

Private, after school, before December 1, nothing on his record, in writing tonight. I'll take it to put this behind him, not because that essay is anything but Owen's. And whether he was heard before the zero is still waiting for an answer, in that same email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight and reply to your email. Put Thursday the twelfth in it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school before December 1, tentatively Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in Owen's record. I still require a direct answer on whether Owen was spoken to before the zero was entered on November 3. I expect all of this from you in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite after school before December 1 with nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight and a straight answer on whether Owen was heard first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached with time to spare.
What moved her: letting her search the play herself for the line the essay quoted, because she could check it with her own eyes and her misremembering defence had no answer.
What cost ground: stepping around her question about whether Owen was spoken to before the zero, more than once, because each dodge made her sharper and the point is still open in her email.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's creation between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, a late October night close to what she saw; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer yes or no right away and own it if the answer was no, the same way you owned the phone call at the start.
